label: copy-phase onset (<DEL> step) in long sequences, content-modulated
explanation: Never fires in the original phase. 80% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0) and nearly all the rest is on the first copy step (recall_idx 1); a few hits at recall_idx 2. Firing rate climbs steeply with sequence length (to_go 8: 13%, to_go 7: 7%, short sequences almost never), so L=8-9 hold about 80% of the mass. Which delimiter steps fire depends on content in a distributed way: rates are higher when the first original token (the token being output) is c, f, 0 or z, and when the sequence contains several of h, d, i, v, y, x. The top activations are <DEL> steps of L=9 sequences starting with c/f/z. No small set of tokens gives high precision: even among L>=8 delimiter steps only about 21% fire. Dev scores: phase==1 gives mass recall 0.80 at precision 0.09; the recorded predicate gives F1 0.375 and mass recall 0.70.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: c, f, 0, z; copy phase: 0, f, c, z; input phase: ) and the third original token (most: h, d, i, y, x, 0; least: z, a, p, o); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, to_go=7, L=9 & t=10.
